teams.synopsis: I don’t know how sustainable this success is with the injuries and the WR2, TE, and FLEX being fluky, but it’s working for now and who says it won’t continue.
teams.blurb: We have a new team on the throne. Rolls With Butter is a peculiar case, on one hand the team leads the league in points scored and they’re 2-0, but on the other hand they are dealing with so many injuries and are projected to be one of the lowest scoring teams in the league. Looking at the team, they’re kind of just a four-headed monster at this point, but those four have been incredible. I don’t know how sustainable this success is with the injuries and the WR2, TE, and FLEX being fluky, but it’s working for now and who says it won’t continue. Anthony is projected to have the hardest strength of schedule for the rest of the season and a tough matchup in Week 3, but he’s proved me wrong before. For the moment being, this is the team to beat. [[img:anthony_01]] [[img:anthony_02]]

teams.synopsis: Led by Davante Adams 39.5 points in Week 2, which is the franchise’s 6th most points scored by a player in a single game, N.Y. Routensss put the entire league on notice with their SNF and MNF comeback.
teams.blurb: One of the biggest risers in this week’s rankings, Andrew deserves his flowers after being the highest scoring team in Week 2. Led by Davante Adams 39.5 points in Week 2, which is the franchise’s 6th most points scored by a player in a single game, N.Y. Routensss put the entire league on notice with their SNF and MNF comeback. [[img:andrew_01]] It’s kind of crazy because this team still has room for improvement. Justin Jefferson was disappointing in the bad weather game, the WR5 is sitting on Andrew’s bench, and the Kicker and D/ST combined for less than six points in Week 2. The team is projected to obliterate their opponent in Week 3, based on ESPN’s projections, but even without those I think this is shaping up to be a fun week for the team. Also, fun note for Andrew, with the win in Week 2 the team now moves to 7-0 all-time in Week 2 matchups. They were inevitable. [[img:andrew_02]] [[img:andrew_03]]

teams.synopsis: The team is projected to score the most points in Week 3, alone with N.Y. Routensss as the only two teams to be projected to score over 120 points this week.
teams.blurb: After raving about this team in last week’s rankings they went out and put up less than 100 points in a loss, come on brother. Despite that poor performance I still have them as a top ranked team heading into Week 3. The team is projected to score the most points in Week 3, alone with N.Y. Routensss as the only two teams to be projected to score over 120 points this week. [[img:charlie_01]] I talked about Aidan having some of the best depth in the league, well Charlie is up there too. On paper the team looks like it has no holes, but we’ve seen how flaky David Montgomery and the WR duo of Drake London and George Pickens can be. However, I think those players are primed for a bounce back going forward. I’m obviously hesitant to drop this team further down the rankings, but if they repeat their Week 2 performance in Week 3 then uncomfortable conversations will need to be had, but I don’t see that happening. The team is also projected to have the 2nd easiest strength of schedule rest of season, Week 3 will be very telling in how we should view No Fox Gibbs’en. [[img:charlie_02]]

teams.synopsis: Interestingly enough, this feeling isn’t new for Aidan as he came into 2026 with the worst schedule luck in league history, with 7 wins less than expected from 2021-2025.
teams.blurb: Back up to 4th after dropping down a few spots. Despite the close loss to N.Y. Routensss in Week 2 I moved Aidan up, which I feel is fair for a team that dropped the 2nd most points on the week. Interestingly enough, this feeling isn’t new for Aidan as he came into 2026 with the worst schedule luck in league history, with 7 wins less than expected from 2021-2025. [[img:aidan_01]] Unfortunately, ESPN predicts the losing to continue in Week 3, but we’ll see what happens. I won’t put Aidan on prime time this week with the Matchup of the Week, maybe the lights are a little too bright. Chris Olave and Ja’Marr Chase is as good as it gets at the WR position, while the rest of the starting lineup seems like it’s in a good place. Maybe the FLEX has been shaky, but I’d say Aidan has some of the best depth in the entire league so that fix shouldn’t be hard to make. Let’s see if the team can get their 1st win of 2026, their 1st win since Week 10 of 2025, and their 3rd win since Week 11 of 2024… sheesh I just got sad typing that out.

teams.synopsis: I don’t really see any holes in the roster.
teams.blurb: No change in rank for Ben this week. I have similar thoughts on Ben’s team as I had for Brandon’s team above, but I just think the ceiling is higher for this team. Like I said in my Week 2 ranking for this team, I don’t really see any holes in the roster. The team has a star WR, a star RB, a star QB, and then serviceable depth for both RB and WR. I also believe Kyle Pitts will bounce back with Michael Penix Jr. in Week 3 and beyond, so Ben won’t have as much uncertainty with that position moving forward. It also doesn’t hurt to have an advantage at D/ST. ESPN projects it to be a rough week for the team against Make Fantasy Great Again, but I can see those projections being wrong and Ben continuing his undefeated 2026 season. [[img:ben_01]]

teams.synopsis: We just haven’t seen anything from the WR duo of Rashee Rice and Rome Odunze and now I fear Kenneth Walker’s arrival may have dropped Rashee Rice to a top 20 WR at best and the Caleb Williams injury may handicap Rome Odunze in an already packed receiving corps.
teams.blurb: I just have a feeling Brandon won’t be happy with this ranking, but when is he ever? The team is 2-0, but they’re middle of the pack in terms of points per game and we’ve yet to see a true “ceiling” game where the team looks unbeatable. I’ll give it to them, they have a high floor with the RB duo of Jonathan Taylor and Kyren Williams, Jalen Hurts has been great, and the Patriots defense looks to be a true advantage at the position. However, we just haven’t seen anything from the WR duo of Rashee Rice and Rome Odunze and now I fear Kenneth Walker’s arrival may have dropped Rashee Rice to a top 20 WR at best and the Caleb Williams injury may handicap Rome Odunze in an already packed receiving corps. Brandon is projected to lose by A LOT against Charlie in Week 3, but if the concerns I talked above dissipate during this week’s games then he definitely has a chance. The easiest projected strength of schedule also could help the team continue their strong start to the 2026 campaign after Week 3. [[img:brandon_01]] [[img:brandon_02]]

teams.synopsis: The main difference was that both the team’s stars were even better in Week 2 and Harrison Butker added some production for a change.
teams.blurb: Like the team above, Baylen jumps many spots after a solid Week 2 performance. Similar to Week 1, the team was led by the duo of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Brock Purdy with some production from Tyler Warren mixed in. The main difference was that both the team’s stars were even better in Week 2 and Harrison Butker added some production for a change. How sustainable is this recipe for success? I guess we will see the answer to that in Week 3 and beyond with a tougher projected matchup against The Gegwich Effect and one of the harder strength of schedules. Rumor has it this team may be adding Jalen Coker, but for what remains to be seen. Can Station Grits continue the dominant performance in Week 3? [[img:baylen_01]] [[img:baylen_02]]

teams.synopsis: The RB2 slot has yielded the team the lowest points from the slot out of all teams in the league through two weeks.
teams.blurb: A big riser after a strong Week 2 win. Deniz earned his first win of the season as he scored 123.51 points, his most in a single week since Week 8 of 2025. The performance was fueled by his top four players once again, but also some contributions from Xavier Worthy. [[img:deniz_01]] The team is once again projected to win in Week 3 against a struggling opponent. I may sound like a broken record, but will we see Deniz address the RB2 concerns in the coming weeks? The RB2 slot has yielded the team the lowest points from the slot out of all teams in the league through two weeks. The Kicker position has also only given Deniz four points total through two weeks, which is something that’s bound to change with the new kicker acquisition. After being ranked 14th and 13th to start the season, I think this ranking is more accurate for the team’s performance going forward.

teams.synopsis: Currently, I am projected to score the 3rd most points in Week 3 against a team I have yet to lose to in the league’s 7-year history.
teams.blurb: Down I fall. I thought the Zay Flowers hamstring and the De’Zhaun Stribling foot injuries were painful, but losing my 5th round pick for the season? I will miss you Jaxson Dart. Looking forward, Bo Nix was drafted for this very reason, but he’s been disappointing so far, can he turn it around? On paper, I like my team, but Tucker Kraft’s underwhelming performances can only earn him a starting spot for so long. Currently, I am projected to score the 3rd most points in Week 3 against a team I have yet to lose to in the league’s 7-year history. Let’s see how Week 3 goes. [[img:ethan_01]] [[img:ethan_02]]

teams.synopsis: He’s projected to score above average compared to the rest of the league in Week 3 and I just think this roster as currently constructed can give people a run for their money each week.
teams.blurb: He’s climbing, maybe this time next week he’ll be in the top eight for Week 4 rankings. Make Fantasy Great Again has scored the 3rd fewest points in the league through two weeks and has an 0-2 record, so why do I have him ranked as the 5th lowest team? Well, he’s projected to score above average compared to the rest of the league in Week 3 and I just think this roster as currently constructed can give people a run for their money each week. [[img:ryan_01]] I don’t think this roster as of today is built to contend, unless some breakouts happen like Jadarian Price or Brian Thomas Jr., but I do see them being good enough to drop 110-120 points weekly. Week 3 will be crucial for this team’s 2026 outlook, a win can make their lives much easier later in the season, but a loss would immediately send the team down the wrong path. Take advantage of the 5-point spread, don’t fall to 0-3, don’t let the defense defenders break your spirit.

teams.synopsis: I actually shocked myself with this stat, but I thought Quin’s 91.38-point win had to be down there in terms of points scored in a win but actually it was only the 23rd lowest points scored in a win in league history, playoffs included, out of 624 matchups.
teams.blurb: No change in ranking for Quin as we head into the 3rd week of the season. It was a great day for Devonta Smith on Sunday, as he bounced back and put up 27.7 points in a win for both the Eagles and The Gegwich Effect. Now, the only real bright spot in Week 2 for Quin was Brandon Aubrey returning to his usual self, the rest of the team, starting lineup and bench, looked very poor and tried their best to lose Quin his Week 2 matchup. I actually shocked myself with this stat, but I thought Quin’s 91.38-point win had to be down there in terms of points scored in a win but actually it was only the 23rd lowest points scored in a win in league history, playoffs included, out of 624 matchups. A win is a win. [[img:quin_01]] It will be interesting to see how Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers look with Jameis Winston at the helm, since those two will be key pieces in Quin’s hunt for his first Preach Fantasy championship. We know how I feel about Quinshon Judkins, but that could change this week against a weaker run defense. Quin will also need Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense to get going if he wants to be considered a top team in this league, but the easier strength of schedule should help him along that journey.

teams.synopsis: The team’s 57.87-point performance in Week 2 was the franchise’s first time scoring less than 70 points in a single week, excluding playoff games.
teams.blurb: The biggest faller of the week, Carmine had one of his worst weeks ever. In fact, the team’s 57.87-point performance in Week 2 was the franchise’s first time scoring less than 70 points in a single week, excluding playoff games. [[img:carmine_01]] I was very high on Carmine coming into the season and then even higher going into Week 2, but now with injury uncertainty surrounding DJ Moore and Nico Collins, no consistent FLEX player as of Week 3, and Drake Maye looking absolutely horrible up until now, I think moving the team far down the rankings is the right call to make. When the team is healthy and players other than the RB duo start to produce, I believe they can be right back up into the top 5, but until then 12th feels fair. The tough projected strength of schedule also doesn’t make me feel good about Breece’s Pieces outlook, let’s see how things shake out in Week 3 against what is projected to be an easier matchup. [[img:carmine_02]]

teams.synopsis: You have the two draft picks with the lowest surplus value in 2026, basically Colston Loveland and Marvin Harrison Jr. have been the worst picks given where Max took them compared to all picks from 2020-2026.
teams.blurb: A big fall for Max after Week 2, but that’s what happens when you score 70 points and you start dealing with injuries to a top TE, a top QB, and potentially your 1st round pick. It also doesn’t help when, not counting injuries, you have the two draft picks with the lowest surplus value in 2026, basically Colston Loveland and Marvin Harrison Jr. have been the worst picks given where Max took them compared to all picks from 2020-2026. That will surely change as we move through the season, but that can’t feel good if you’re Max. [[img:max_01]] On the bright side, Bryce Young looks like a fine replacement for Caleb Williams while he misses time and Derrick Henry is on pace to lead the NFL in rushing touchdowns this season. A lot will fall on the shoulders of the WR trio of Tee Higgins, Matthew Golden, and KC Concepcion in Week 3 and potentially beyond. A win in Week 3 would be helpful for getting the team back on track, but historically it’s been a tough matchup for Max. [[img:max_02]]

teams.synopsis: The team is uninspiring and missing that superstar to get them 20+ points/week.
teams.blurb: Falling to 0-2 for the 4th time in seven years, Cole has had a rough start to his 2026 campaign. For starters, he was hit with the injury bug to a few key players, most notably Puka Nacua and Jayden Daniels. Combine that with mediocre play from the RB spots through the first two weeks and you get yourself a 14th ranked team. Now, Puka Nacua could be back as early as Week 3 and the WR depth of Ladd McConkey, Josh Downs, Stefon Diggs, and Devaughn Vele is very serviceable, so if the team continues to lose I don’t think it will be because of that position. Essentially, the team is uninspiring and missing that superstar to get them 20+ points/week, a Puka Nacua shaped lifeline is needed. The Week 3 matchup will be difficult on its own, and the tough rest of season strength of schedule doesn’t give me much hope, but maybe this miserable team can shock us? [[img:cole_01]]

matchup_of_the_week.blurb: The Matchup of the Week from Week 2 did not disappoint with the two highest scoring team going against each other and Andrew completing the crazy comeback on Monday night. For this week’s matchup I decided to choose the matchup between the 10th and 5th ranked teams in the Week 3 rankings. Ben and Ryan have met six times in league history, with Ryan coming out victorious five of those six times, and he’s favored to do it again. Ryan’s dealing with some injuries that we’ll have to keep an eye on, but when healthy I think he has the balanced team here while Ben has more star power and a higher ceiling. Let’s hope for a repeat of last week’s prime time game!
